high-severity-risks-mitigated.reason: RESTORED 2026-08-26 BY THE EXIT CONDITION THIS ATTESTATION WROTE FOR ITSELF, not by a fresh judgement of whether the risk still matters. The previous reason said this returns to satisfied when QST-0023 produces a production-safe design AND that design is validated — an artifact-reading route measured to reflect an external write under `next build` + `next start`. Both halves have now happened, in that order, and the condition is being executed rather than reinterpreted. ⚠️ THE DESIGN: DEC-0019. Every server-side planning-content read awaits `connection()` before the filesystem read, inside a `<Suspense>` boundary whose fallback is a real loading state. Chosen for independence from the Cache Components setting rather than for freshness alone — EVD-0023 measured three mechanisms that are fresh and only this one is fresh in both caching models, so the contract does not quietly depend on a flag nobody has decided. ⚠️ THE VALIDATION: EVD-0024, recorded as AST-0021 at rung 4. The contract route served the externally written values on every request after a write made while the server was live, with cacheComponents both enabled and disabled, and its Suspense fallback was present in the initial HTML — so the loading state the contract requires was observed, not assumed. A NEGATIVE CONTROL in the same build made the same reads without the contract and was stale in both configurations. Without that control a fresh result could not be distinguished from a build that happened to be dynamic, and this criterion would have been restored on a demonstration. ⚠️ WHAT SATISFIED MEANS HERE, STATED SO IT IS NOT READ AS MORE. It means the register's one outstanding high-severity row has a mitigation that has been run, which is what this criterion asks at a stage that precedes any implementation. It does NOT mean the application implements the contract: no application shell exists yet. That obligation is real and it belongs to stage 7's acceptance criteria, not here — a stage-6 criterion stretched to cover implementation would block on work stage 6 does not do. ⚠️ AST-0022 HANDS STAGE 7 A CONSTRAINT, and it is the reason to read that assertion before writing the criteria. A non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so a violation passes every behavioural freshness check until the compliant sibling moves — at which point every read on the route silently reverts to build-time content. The contract's per-read clause forecloses that, but only if it is enforced STATICALLY. An acceptance criterion that tests output freshness would report success on a codebase that violates the contract. ⚠️ REGRESSES AGAIN if the shell is built on a per-route reading of DEC-0019, if the prefetch cost is measured to be worse than the documentation implies and the contract is revisited, or on an upgrade beyond Next.js 16.3.2 — the same reopening clause AST-0010 carried, which fired once already and is the reason this round happened at all.
